item.title: THEATER REVIEW: Barrington Stage Company’s 2026 10×10 New Play Festival plays through March 15
item.description: This is two hours of joy that warms up a wintry day, and it is something that everyone who enjoys good theater should see.

item.title: BITS & BYTES: Julian Brave NoiseCat at Spencertown Academy; Daniel Kleederman at Studio 9; New Black Eagle Jazz Band at Proprietor’s Lodge; ‘BLKNWS: Terms & Conditions’ at The Triplex; Elizabeth Diggs at Spencertown Academy; Living in Recovery concert
item.description: The “Coyote Story,” an art form once practiced by Indigenous peoples from Central America to Western Canada, is one of the oldest and most significant oral traditions in human history.

item.title: Cheryl Ann (Wallis) Lanoue, 67, of Great Barrington
item.description: Calling hours will be held on Thursday, Feb. 19, 2026, at Finnerty & Stevens Funeral Home. Visiting hours for immediate and extended family will be from 3 to 5 p.m., and for community friends from 5 to 7 p.m.

item.title: James Carl ‘Jim’ Daily, 77, of Stockbridge
item.description: A celebration of life for Jim will be held in the spring of 2026.

item.title: Robert Alvin White Jr., 78, of Lenox
item.description: In lieu of flowers, donations can be directed to Beacon Center in Madison, Wis., where his niece Sara dedicated her time to supporting the unhoused; the Sara Marie White Memorial Epilepsy Scholarship; or the restoration of the Lenox Meeting house.

item.title: In pursuit of Black History: NAACP Berkshires discusses 10 Million Names Project at Black History Month meeting
item.description: The goal of the genealogical project is to recover the names and histories of the estimated 10 million people of African descent who were enslaved between the 1500s and 1865 on land that became the United States.

item.title: FILM REVIEW: Petra Volpe’s ‘Late Shift’
item.description: The film focuses completely on Floria (Leonie Benesch), a single-mom nurse who works under intense pressure to handle an overload of patients. She is compassionate and conscientious but also capable of making mistakes and losing control with one patient.

item.title: STEPHEN COHEN: Bella Italy
item.description: Italians are fascinated by Trump. Tuscany is very liberal, but even my more conservative friends here and in Sicily and Milan cannot understand why he continually changes his policies on a daily basis.

item.title: BITS & BYTES: Hub New Music at The Clark; Chrissi Poland at Indigo Room; Curious Festival of Unfinished Works at Adams Theater; Abir Saksouk at Fisher Center; Bonney Hartley at MCLA; Jurian Hughes at Wander
item.description: This immersive new work seamlessly blends electronic and acoustic sounds, and is inspired by the cultural phenomena surrounding UFO-sightings.

item.title: THE LAZY BERKSHIRE GARDENER: Week of February 19, 2026
item.description: Even if you do not consider yourself a garden designer, you can plant with intention.
